title: The projector compared only the card record, so a change of the task detail alone appended no card-changed, though wire contracts sections 8 and 10 require one
resolution: The stored projection is the card with its task detail, a fleet obstacle's observation time stripped, and the event still carries the card; a projector test of a later stage's gate and an admission change fails before the fix (fb-15-p1-1.log); the design and the delta say so.

title: A reservation held or released touched only its own task's card, though every waiting card's fleet obstacle reads the workers' free slots
resolution: Assignment triggers write a fleet touch when a held reservation is inserted, released, or moved to another worker, and a fleet touch names every card; a PostgreSQL test with two cards fails before the fix (fb-15-p1-2.log).

title: No trigger watched the admissions that the task detail shows, so an admission-only write scheduled no projection
resolution: An admissions trigger writes an admission touch, which take() maps to the cards of the tasks that name the admission; a PostgreSQL test fails before the fix (fb-15-p1-3.log).

title: No trigger watched the installation quarantine and recovery epoch that every fleet obstacle reads
resolution: Installation triggers write a fleet touch on insert and on a change of the quarantine or the recovery epoch, not of the identity; a PostgreSQL test fails before the fix (fb-15-p1-4.log).

title: Any session of the task made an active attempt working, so a stopped session of an earlier attempt showed a retry awaiting placement as working
resolution: A task is working only while a session binds its active attempt or still runs a generation of it, otherwise stopped; a view test of a stopped earlier session with a new retry fails before the fix (fb-15-p1-5.log).

title: The task detail lists tasks by task identifier, while product ports section 3.7 and TaskDetail.tasks require admission order
resolution: Per the coordinator decision of 2026-11-03, the tasks INSERT takes admission_seq from a PostgreSQL sequence, backfilled in task identifier order, and the card lists its tasks by the path of sequences from the root (design decision 10); tests fail before the fix (fb-15-p1-6.log).

title: A card waiting for a person still showed a waiting placement obstacle, which product ports section 3.3 allows only while it waits for capacity
resolution: The card shows its first rejected obstacle, else its first waiting one only while waitingFor is capacity, and each task in the detail keeps its own; a view test fails before the fix (fb-15-p1-7.log).

title: The numbering test expected the projected event to be numbered at once, which an older transaction of another test database prevents
resolution: The test waits on the numbering horizon condition, numbers through the READ COMMITTED production log, and a new test holds an older transaction open to show the event waits for it; the old test fails with such a transaction (fb-15-p1-8.log).

title: The in-memory catalog kept a title with an unpaired surrogate that PostgreSQL text replaced, so the two adapters did not round-trip alike
resolution: parseCardRecord refuses an unpaired surrogate, so both adapters accept only titles that PostgreSQL keeps; the shared conformance case fails before the fix on both adapters (fb-15-p1-9.log), and reads back an astral title unchanged.

title: The design said the inbox counts count by kind, while InboxCounts has total and byCard
resolution: Design decision 6 describes total and byCard.

title: The design said every write of the empty merge queue answers unavailable, while transition answers not-found
resolution: Design decision 3 names unavailable for enqueue and recordManualMerge and not-found for transition and latestForRun.

title: One card whose view could not be read failed the whole projection batch, so no card event of the installation was appended until a manual repair
resolution: An unreadable card appends nothing and gets a new run touch above the pass horizon, so it stays pending and retries next pass, while the other cards project; the numbering pass logs only run identifiers and a count; a PostgreSQL test with a card without its run fails before (fb-15-p2-1.log).

title: A worker or fleet touch reprojected every card of the installation in one SERIALIZABLE transaction, which concurrent writers could keep aborting
resolution: A pass first expands project, worker, and fleet touches into one run touch per card, then projects at most 100 touches per transaction up to that horizon, each batch consuming its touches with its events; a fleet crash test over 101 cards fails before (fb-15-p2-2.log).

title: The worker update trigger fired on columns the board does not read, and no watched table but placement outcomes touched on delete
resolution: The worker trigger compares only the placement record fields and whether the worker is enrolled, read through the row so earlier down migrations still run, and every watched table but the cards also touches on delete; a PostgreSQL test fails before (fb-15-p2-3.log).

title: The admission order contract lived only in the PostgreSQL adapter, with a test double as the in-memory half of the parity test
resolution: CardCatalog gains tasks(runId); the in-memory catalog orders the lineage by the admission path as PostgreSQL does, and a lineage conformance case on both adapters fails before in memory (fb-15-p2-4.log). It overlaps the coordinator parity constraint, fixed in the same commit.

title: The record was said to cite an item 14 helper, untilNumberable, that item 14 does not have
resolution: The claim is wrong: item 14 exports untilNumberable from packages/adapters/postgres/test/test-database.ts at line 121 of the base 468783d9, built on untilHorizonAbove with the same query, so the citation is accurate and stays.

title: take ran the card resolution query even when it removed no touch
resolution: take answers an empty batch before the resolution query; an efficiency change without a behaviour change, so it has no fail-before test, and the empty take is asserted.

title: The card index used the database collation while the board sorts run identifiers by C, and the admission sequence had no owner
resolution: The index sorts run_id COLLATE C and the sequence is owned by tasks.admission_seq, so the down migration drops it with the column; a PostgreSQL test fails before (fb-15-p2-7.log). The project references stay out: each down migration must run over every later table, and item 25 owns the card intake.

title: A session on an unreachable worker without a recorded contact showed as working
resolution: An unreachable owning worker answers worker-unreachable with its last contact, or stopped without one; a view test fails before (fb-15-p2-8.log), and design decision 4 says so.
